idiom.note: raw pinned threads + one bounded SPSC ring per (worker, worker) pair; actor i is owned by worker i % cores; not an actor framework and not ranked as one

caveats: THIS IS NOT A FRAMEWORK. Actors are integers, a hop is one ring push and one ring pop, and there is no scheduler: the floor for a hand-off, not for finding the next actor
actor i lives on worker i % cores, so with cores=2 every hop crosses a core -- the same placement qb gets, and the worst case for a shard-per-core design
cores=1 is one thread pushing the token into its own ring and popping it back -- the floor for single-threaded dispatch, still a real queue
wait=1 busy-polls the rings; wait=0 parks an idle worker on a condition variable, which with one token and two workers means one park and one wake per hop
